messages:
arya: Heads-up — finished the mixed-load run against staging runtime v2.13 and seeing a 3x tail latency regression at p99 when continuous batching is enabled. Repro steps + logs below, looking for quick triage help.

mike: yikes. is this only with continuous batching or also with fixed batching?

arya: only continuous. fixed batching (batch cap=32, no delay) looks fine. continuous config used: max_batch_size=128, max_delay_ms=12, kv_cache_enabled=true. run command: `rli bench --replay traces/2026-03-15.json --model redwood-13b --runtime v2.13 --continuous-batching=true --max-delay-ms=12 --max-batch-size=128`.

jess: can you paste profiler snippet? also: was this with the same kernel selection as baseline? kernel autotuner sometimes flips to fused attention for seq=2048 which can spike.

arya: pasted relevant lines from perf output:\n```\n[1749001234] PROFILE SUMMARY
throughput_tokens/s: 12000 -> expected 14000
p50_ms: 28
p95_ms: 160
p99_ms: 430  <-- regressed (baseline p99 ~140)
KV_CACHE_HITRATE: 0.72
KERNEL: attention_fused_v2 selected by autotuner for batch_size=64 seq_len=1024
GPU_UTIL: 89% -> baseline 87%
```\n
mike: KV hitrate 0.72 seems low for replay. was the trace replay preserving arrival timestamps and prompt prefixes? if replay batches more heterogeneous seq lengths, autotuner might pick a kernel that is bad for mixed shapes.

arya: replay harness used `--preserve-arrival=true` and captured token lengths. I also did a synthetic Poisson generator with same QPS and got smaller tails. so difference between synthetic vs replay.

olivia: that points to batching heuristics + queueing fairness. continuous batching will wait up to max_delay_ms to collect requests and then form a batch; a handful of long-seq requests can block earlier short requests inside the same scheduling window which increases p99. We should check per-batch shape distribution and if we allow shape heterogeneity inside a batch.

jess: we should also ensure apples-to-apples: same model artifact, same quantization, same kernels pinned. autotuner can change between runs. For an apples-to-apples benchmark pin `KERNEL_HINT=attention_unfused` env var or use `--force-kernel` in bench harness.

mike: agreed. action list: 1) rerun replay with kernel pinned to baseline, 2) collect batch shape histogram, 3) run with KV cache disabled to isolate cache effect, 4) run with max_delay_ms stepped (0,4,8,12,20) and record p50/p95/p99.

arya: started 1 and 3. quick results: pin kernel to attention_unfused -> p99 drops to ~150 (close to baseline). disable kv cache -> p99 ~140. So kernel choice is the dominant factor here. But why did autotuner pick fused_v2?

sam_perf_bot: autotuner picks kernel based on historical median seq_len and batch_size profile from the last 5 minutes. If incoming distribution changed (more long sequences) and mixed-shape batches are frequent, fused_v2 gave better avg throughput but terrible tail latency for mixed shapes.

olivia: that explains tradeoff: autotuner optimizes throughput (avg) sometimes at the cost of tail latency. For production SLOs we should add objective weighting for tail (p99) or add a policy: prefer unfused for heterogeneous batches or when continuous batching is on.

jess: For continuous batching heuristics we can improve fairness by: a) separating queue by sequence-length buckets (short/long) and maintain per-bucket max_delay_ms, b) introduce a per-tenant max_wait_ms to avoid head-of-line blocking, c) cap batch heterogeneity: only allow shapes that differ by <= 16 tokens in same batch.

mike: also consider dynamic max_batch_size that shrinks when variance(seq_len) in queue is high. Implementation: `effective_batch_size = min(max_batch_size, max_capacity_for_shape_variance(variance))`.

arya: wrote a quick config prototype for queue shaping:\n```\nqueue_policy: {
  buckets: [ {name: short, max_len: 128, max_delay_ms: 8, max_batch_size: 128},
             {name: medium, max_len: 512, max_delay_ms: 12, max_batch_size: 64},
             {name: long, max_len: 2048, max_delay_ms: 20, max_batch_size: 8} ]
  fairness: weighted_round_robin(true)
  tenant_max_wait_ms: 200
}
```\n
olivia: nice. Also add KV-aware routing: if a request misses the KV cache heavily, treat it as `cold` (lower expected throughput) and prefer unfused kernel or smaller pack sizes. That way warms aren't penalized.

jess: Regarding benchmark methodology notes for the docs/bench repo: we need reproducible runs: pin model artifact sha, seed, tokenizer version, kernel selection, and replay trace. Use `--warmup=300s` to stabilize autotuner state or `--cold-start=true` to measure cold behavior. Always report both.

mike: important apples-to-apples checklist: 1) same model file/quantization, 2) same cuda/cuDNN/cuBLAS driver versions, 3) same runtime flags (kv cache, beam, sampling), 4) same arrival patterns (replay vs synthetic documented), 5) kernel pinning or note autotuner window.

arya: I'm going to: A) add kernel-pinning to the replay harness so we can bisect autotuner flip. B) add a per-batch shape histogram exporter to telemetry (buckets: mean_len, stddev_len, max_len, n_items). C) run staircase max_delay_ms test to find knee for p99 vs throughput.

olivia: one more test: tenant fairness under mixed-tenancy. Create two synthetic tenants: tenant-A short-only high QPS, tenant-B long-only low QPS. Replay arrival mixed into one queue and measure per-tenant p95/p99. We should assert tenant-A p99 doesn't blow up when tenant-B has occasional long requests.

sam_perf_bot: scheduling test harness snippet: `rli bench --replay traces/multi_tenant.json --tenants tenantA,tenantB --continuous-batching --max-delay-ms=12 --export batch_shapes.json`

jess: put a regression detector in CI: baseline run artifacts stored, and new builds must run a short replay (1 hour) with pinned kernel+replay trace and compare p50/p95/p99 within thresholds. If p99 increases by >20% trigger alert.

mike: +1. Also add an integration test that simulates mixed shapes and asserts kernel autotuner doesn't flip to a kernel that worsens p99 by >x% across the last N decisions. We can simulate autotuner decisions by feeding synthetic shape distributions.

arya: thanks all — I'll push the telemetry change and the replay harness kernel pin PR. tagging @jess for kernel autotuner tweak follow-up and @olivia for queue policy review. Will post results of the max_delay sweep in this thread. :thumbsup:

olivia: thanks — appreciate the quick triage. keep us posted.

(THREAD ENDS)
